Example 2 · Combinatorics

5 People in a Row — A and B Cannot Stand Together

The challenge

Count valid arrangements where two specific people cannot be adjacent — a classic problem that is easy to miscount.

How Tutorly solves it

  1. Visualizes all 120 permutations
  2. Highlights the forbidden “block” case
  3. Applies the block method step by step: 4! · 2! = 48
  4. Independently verifies 120 − 48 = 72 by brute-force enumeration in Python — not by trusting the model

Architecture

From Problem to Lesson: The Full Pipeline

Inspired by LLM2Manim (arXiv:2604.05266), Tutorly uses a plan-first architecture with structured scenes, independent validation, and a feedback loop that regenerates only failed stages — not the entire lesson.

🧠 Gemini 3.8 Flash drives every reasoning stage · 🐍 Python checks every output before it moves on

The brain

Gemini 3.8 Flash: The Multimodal Brain Behind Every Stage

Google's multimodal Gemini model does the thinking — understanding, solving, teaching and designing. It always answers in typed, structured JSON, so every output can be checked by code before the next stage uses it.

Gemini doesProducesChecked by
Understands the problemProblemIR + ScopeIR: givens, unknowns, allowed methods✓ Scope Validator: high-school level, learner's range
Solves it, step by stepSolutionIR with the reason for every step✓ SymPy + NetworkX / brute force
Plans the lessonscenes, concepts, notation ledger✓ Ledger Validator: consistent notation across scenes
Writes the narrationspoken explanation, high-school language✓ language & jargon checks
Designs the visualssemantic visual plan: presets + operations✓ geometry & layout validator
Answers questionschat answer or a new video lesson✓ same validated pipeline

Gemini is creative, Python is strict — the model proposes, code verifies.

Design rationale

Why Not Just LLM → Manim?

✗ The risk of direct code generation

problem→LLM→Manim code

Feeding a problem straight to an LLM for Manim code can produce wrong formulas, inconsistent narration and unstable animations — with no way to isolate the failure.

✓ Tutorly's separation of concerns

Mathematical reasoning⟷didactic planning
Narrative⟷semantic visual plan
  • ✓Each stage validated independently; failures trigger local regeneration only
  • ✓Manim code passes AST validation and runs in a sandboxed, offline process
  • ✓Every attempt, error and result is logged in SQLite — AI with accountability, not a black box

A broken animation never touches the verified mathematics — only that scene is regenerated.

Follow-up questions

Every Student Question Becomes a New Video Lesson

When a student asks “Why can't we just count all arrangements?”, Tutorly uses the scene context, the knowledge scope and the concept ledger to answer in chat — and, when a picture is needed, generates a personalised animated explanation through the same validated pipeline.
